ca_north_ridge_4.descent_text: From the summit, hike southwest down to the plateau and cross it until you find a west-facing scree gully; several gullies look alike from above, and picking the wrong one is the usual mistake, so check the line from the valley beforehand. Once you are in the right one, the whole line down is visible. Early in the season, or after a big winter, the gully may hold snow or ice that calls for an ice axe and crampons. At the bottom you pass Grass Lake and rejoin the Meysan Lakes trail, which switchbacks down to the Whitney Portal campground.
ca_north_ridge_4.approach: The approach starts at the Meysan Lake trailhead at the south end of the Whitney Portal campground, where the Meysan Lakes trail climbs steadily in switchbacks. Lone Pine Peak comes into view to the southeast. Leave the trail well below the lakes, cross the slabs toward Meysan Creek, then follow moraine to a break in the northwest face. A use trail and easy class 2 terrain angle up and left to the north ridge, which you follow to the notch where the climbing begins. The usual bivouac spot, called the Dormitory, sits near the base of the second tower.
